items.title: ByteDance pushed longer one-take video generation
items.oneliner: Seedance 2.5 generates 30-second clips in one pass, pushing AI video from snippets toward editable narrative production.

items.title: AMD showed cheaper Kimi K3 inference
items.oneliner: AMD's MI355X ran Kimi K3 at 952 tok/s per node, making open-model inference economics harder to ignore.

items.title: OpenAI claimed major math breakthroughs
items.oneliner: OpenAI says Astra solved 10 open math and CS problems, which would redefine scientific reasoning if verified.

items.title: Apple patched a pre-auth root RCE
items.oneliner: Apple fixed a Screen Sharing bug letting unauthenticated attackers get root in seconds on macOS 26.5 and earlier.

items.title: Coldcard shipped a low-entropy bug
items.oneliner: A poorly documented Coldcard firmware change weakened randomness, reminding security teams that tiny commits can sink trust.

items.title: TLS 1.2 finally dropped obsolete key exchange
items.oneliner: RFC 10015 deprecates RSA and finite-field Diffie-Hellman in TLS 1.2, closing the door on cipher suites teams should retire.

items.title: Lean fixed a kernel soundness flaw
items.oneliner: Lean patched a bug that accepted proofs of False, a sharp reminder that formal verification stacks still have supply-chain risk.

items.title: Chrome started testing browser-based email verification
items.oneliner: Chrome's Email Verification origin trial could kill OTP tab-switching and make signup funnels less brittle for product teams.

items.title: Europe forced Android interoperability openings
items.oneliner: The EU ordered Google to open 11 Android features, giving assistant and smart-home builders access gatekeepers used to withhold.

items.title: Europe launched a sovereign web index push
items.oneliner: Ecosia and Qwant backed a European web index, signaling that search and AI data infrastructure are becoming geopolitical assets.
